analysis: Both units are head_text for lines 1-792 of docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The file_changes ranges put the PR's edits at head lines 1256 and later (the `darkbloom sandbox setup --disk <volume>` option and its Setup text). Nothing in lines 1-792 falls inside a changed range, so these units are unchanged surrounding context. I found no security regression in them and no pre-existing issue to report as new. The surrounding text is documentation only. It describes cache storage (`darkbloom cache set --directory`, with volume UUID pinning and invalid storage disabling SSD caching, consistent with T-041 and CacheVolume checks), logout and token handling, the App Attest and legacy trust display, and add-on hold flags. None of it conflicts with the base threat model. The PR's real change is outside the supplied units. `setup --disk` adds operator-supplied paths that are passed to the downloaded installer. It touches TB-013 and T-061 (the installer and add-on run as the Mac owner) and A-019. The new text is not visible here, so I cannot check that path validation (absolute paths, `/Volumes` handling, statfs checks, arguments passed to install.sh) matches the documented behavior. I also cannot check that it stays within what the threat model says about the installer. The next pass should review the changed region from line 1256 onward. Specifically: whether `--disk` passes arguments to install.sh safely, whether the `~` handling and the paths are validated, and whether TB-013/T-061 need updating for work disks outside the home directory. This is a documentation-only change, so I did not verify that the code matches the docs.
